extractions.value: Clinical features: continuous right lower limb myoclonus, mild encephalopathy; Antibody: positive anti-GAD65 antibodies; EMG: spontaneous and synchronous activation of right vastus lateralis and biceps femoralis, burst duration 30 ms, frequency about 8 Hz; EEG: mild disorganization of background activity, compatible with mild encephalopathy; CSF: 20 white cells/mm3; Response to treatment: great improvement with intravenous methylprednisolone; Exclusion of mimics: antibodies to NMDAR, LGI1, GABAR, GlyR, AMPAR, and CASPR2 were negative, normal whole-body PET/CT, negative infectious workup.
extractions.quote: Physical examination at rest showed spontaneous, continuous, irregular, low amplitude, involuntary movements limited to the right leg, suggestive of myoclonic jerks ... The patient’s mild bradyphrenia consisted of slowness of thinking and impaired attention ... Serum and CSF autoantibody panel was positive for anti-glutamic acid decarboxylase 65 (anti-GAD) antibodies ... EMG recorded with needle electrodes showed spontaneous and synchronous activation of right vastus lateralis and biceps femoralis. The burst duration was 30 ms, at a frequency of about 8 Hz, suggestive of myoclonus ... EEG was compatible with mild encephalopathy ... the patient was pulsed with 5 g of intravenous methylprednisolone ... with a great improvement in both motor and cognitive symptoms ... Antibodies to NMDAR, LGI1, GABAR, GlyR, AMPAR, and CASPR2 were negative ... Whole-body positron emission tomography/computed tomography scan was normal.

extractions.value: The authors explicitly state that this case should not be classified under the umbrella of SPSDs because there was no clinical stiffness or related neurophysiological findings. The final diagnosis was an anti-GAD antibody-associated neurologic syndrome presenting with limb myoclonus.
extractions.quote: However, there was no clinical stiffness or related neurophysiological findings. In our opinion, it is thus not appropriate to classify this case under the umbrella of SPSDs. Our final diagnosis was an anti-GAD antibody-associated neurologic syndrome presenting with limb myoclonus.
